# 7. Normalized Perception Profile

Vehicles today ship with wildly different sensor suites. A current-generation luxury sedan may carry four radars, a lidar, six cameras, and twelve ultrasonics; a compact EV may carry one forward radar and three cameras; a commercial truck may carry a different superset again. Each suite produces a different native representation of the world: different coordinate frames, different object-class taxonomies, different confidence semantics, different update rates.

The Normalized Perception Profile is the contract that lets all of these produce interoperable output. It is not a least-common-denominator. It is a structured downscale that preserves the information a cooperative peer actually needs and discards the rest.

## 7.1 Reference Frame

All pose and kinematic data in O-CPS messages MUST be expressed in the World Geodetic System 1984 (WGS-84) frame, with latitude and longitude in decimal degrees, altitude in meters above the WGS-84 ellipsoid. Heading (yaw) MUST be expressed in degrees clockwise from true north. Velocity MUST be expressed in meters per second along the heading axis. Deviation from WGS-84 is a conformance failure.

## 7.2 Object Taxonomy

Objects in PerceptionSummary messages MUST be classified into exactly one of the following normalized classes. An implementation MAY maintain a richer internal taxonomy and collapse to this set on the wire.

| **Class ID** | **Name** | **Description** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0x00 | UNKNOWN | An obstacle of indeterminate type. MUST be used when the source cannot confidently classify. |
| 0x01 | PASSENGER_CAR | Light passenger vehicle, including SUVs and light pickups. |
| 0x02 | COMMERCIAL_TRUCK | Medium- or heavy-duty commercial vehicle. |
| 0x03 | BUS | Passenger bus (transit or motorcoach). |
| 0x04 | MOTORCYCLE | Two-wheeled motor vehicle. |
| 0x05 | BICYCLE | Non-motorized or e-bike bicycle with rider. |
| 0x06 | PEDESTRIAN | Human outside any vehicle. |
| 0x07 | ANIMAL | Large animal in or near the roadway. |
| 0x08 | STATIC_OBSTACLE | Non-vehicle, non-living obstacle (debris, cone, barrier). |
| 0x09 | EMERGENCY_VEHICLE | Vehicle with active emergency signaling. MUST be asserted only on direct evidence (e.g., light-bar detection) or on receipt of a corresponding J2735 EVA message. |
| 0x0A | CONSTRUCTION_EQUIPMENT | Non-roadgoing equipment present in or near the roadway. |
| 0x0B-0xFE | RESERVED | Reserved for future assignment by the O-CPS registry. |
| 0xFF | VENDOR_EXTENSION | Vendor-specific class. MUST be accompanied by a vendor OID. Peers MUST ignore if OID is unrecognized. |

## 7.3 Confidence Semantics

Every object in a PerceptionSummary carries a confidence score in the range [0, 255] with the following semantics:

| **Range** | **Label** | **Interpretation** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0–63 | LOW | Source has weak evidence (single modality, short dwell, high ambiguity). Peers MUST NOT use as sole input for safety-critical advisory. |
| 64–127 | MEDIUM | Single-modality or short-dwell detection with corroboration. May be used as supporting evidence for fusion. |
| 128–191 | HIGH | Multi-modality fusion or extended dwell. Suitable as primary input to cooperative behaviors. |
| 192–255 | VERY_HIGH | Multi-modality fusion with independent corroboration and stable track. The source MUST have demonstrated track stability for at least 500 ms. |

Confidence semantics are uniform across implementations: a source reporting HIGH confidence on a P-256 / bicycle-class track at range 40 m MUST have subjected that detection to the same evidentiary standard regardless of which sensor modalities it used. Systematic miscalibration (e.g., a vendor routinely reporting VERY_HIGH on single-modality camera-only detections) is detectable through consensus comparison (§10.3) and is a basis for misbehavior reporting.

## 7.4 Relevance Horizon

Every PerceptionSummary is scoped to a relevance horizon, expressed in meters. Peers MUST NOT consume objects beyond the declared horizon, and transmitters MUST NOT declare a horizon larger than the effective range at which their sensor suite can produce detections at MEDIUM confidence or better. Typical values:

- Urban intersection: 50–100 m
- Arterial road: 100–200 m
- Limited-access highway: 200–400 m
- RSU-sourced perception: up to 500 m, provided the RSU can substantiate the horizon in its conformance report.
